about: Differences that are listed and explained rather than fixed (PLAN P7: a human reviews the differences, and the differences are listed). `rows` explains a report row whose status is `differs`, naming exactly the layers it differs in (`pixels`, `dom`, `meaning`, `behaviour`), so a difference on another layer still fails; `general` lists differences no single row shows. A failed row is never a residual.

general.why: P7 compares screenshots taken in Chromium 141 (Playwright 1.56.1, build 1194). The product ships in Electronite v37, whose Chromium is 138, so the comparison engine is not the shipped one. G2 adds one capture run of the Rust app inside Electronite, compared with the Chromium 141 run of the same build (Q-28).

The machine fingerprint lists every font face and its version, so a font added, removed or upgraded stops pixel comparisons until both sides are captured again on one machine. A fontconfig rule that changes which face draws a fallback glyph without changing the list is not caught.

The project chip's initials take each word's first character. tC4's `w[0]` takes the first UTF-16 unit, so a word that starts outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (a mathematical letter, many CJK extension characters) gives half of a surrogate pair, a broken glyph; the rebuild gives the whole character (`tc_ui::app::shell::project_initials`, test `astral_initial_is_whole`). Every other name gives tC4's initials, JavaScript's `\s` and full upper-casing included.

tC4 composes the Feedback attachment in the page at once, so its Send never waits. The rebuild's server composes it (`feedback/compose`, A5 D8), and Send stays off until the attachment is shown, so nothing is sent that the dialog did not show (`tc_ui::app::feedback::can_send`). A compose that fails says so in the attachment box in the shown language (`feedback.attachmentFailed`), and opening the report again keeps the typed text and composes again (journey `a compose that fails keeps Send off and says so; the next opening keeps the text and composes again`; test `a_kept_report_whose_compose_failed_composes_again_with_its_text`). No baseline screen shows it: tC4 has no compose to wait for or to fail.

A book tile's drafted percentage counts a verse as drafted when its words, trimmed, are neither empty nor ___ (tc_app::drafted, tC4 #572's span rule). tC4 reads a verse's body only up to its first paragraph marker, so a poem verse whose words are on \q lines is undrafted there and drafted here (test a_poem_verse_with_words_counts_as_drafted). No baseline verse is such a verse.

Home lists every folder that holds a project's files but cannot be opened, by name, with the reason in words and no button (B2 D9; APP-DESIGN §4.5), where tC4's listing leaves it off; while one shows, "No projects yet" is not drawn. No scenario holds such a folder, so no row shows it (journey an_unusable_folder_shows_its_name_and_reason_and_opens_nothing; test unusable_folders_are_listed_with_their_reason).

general.why: Choosing a language whose Door43 code a Scripture Burrito cannot hold (about 470, such as acm-x-lebarabic) fills the Code box with a code it can hold that keeps every letter (acm-x-lebarabi-c) and says so in one sentence; when none can be made the box stays empty and the sentence says why. tC4 fills the Door43 code and stores "Undetermined" (#582). No baseline screen chooses a language.

general.why: The sync result names the verses with two alignments to review under its line ("1 verse has two alignments to review.") and offers Review for them, where tC4 4.0 keeps the newest alignment and counts it among the conflicts that kept the newest version (#791; tc_ui test a_verse_with_two_alignments_is_named_and_offers_review). No baseline sync brings an alignment conflict, so no row shows it.

A sync that stops for a reason no other sentence names shows one fixed sentence, before and after the teammates' work was received, where tC4 4.0 shows "The sync stopped: {reason}" with Door43's words or an I/O reason that can name a file (tc_api test io_reason_renders_without_the_path; journey sync-button). No baseline sync stops so.

A check comment still being typed when the checker moves to another check, goes Home or leaves Check is saved with the check it was typed on, as its Done does (the editor leaving saves its text, and a draft of it stays in the buffer until then); tC4 drops it (`tC4:src/views/Check.jsx`, the editor's reset on a new item). Nothing a translator types is lost. No baseline screen has an editor open (journey `check_comment_saved_on_leaving_the_item`; tc-ui test `check_comment_saves_on_done_and_on_the_gate`).

sync-ok-restored.why: Since E1a the sync is real: tC4's steps run against the fake Door43 (two teammates on other computers, each a tc4 signed in as its own user, open the project, change Titus 1:1 from the same version and sync). Three things differ in the DOM and the meaning, each on purpose. (1) Each teammate's text change to an aligned verse also rewrites that verse's alignment, a second change the rebuild counts, so the counts are twice those of tC4's capture, whose scripted teammates changed the text only; what tC4 counts for such an edit was not measured. (2) The two teammates' alignments of 1:1 differ, and the fold still holds them as an alignment conflict, so the toast says "1 verse has two alignments to review". Ruling H5 makes the newest alignment win, with the Received sheet saying what was replaced; that is unit C7b's, and this note goes when it lands. (3) Teammates are named by their Door43 username, which the first sync of each sends at once (Q7, D98), where tC4's fixture had no username and said "Teammate 1". Door43's branch is moved back to before the second teammate's push, and the second sync sends again both changes that push held (its text and its alignment): "Door43 did not have 2 changes from teammates. tC4 sent them again.", where tC4's scripted outcome sent one. The pixels differ by these lines and by ruling Q2 (masked q2-obs-card).

check-error.why: The reason under the failed open: tC4 prints its fetch's error (`Failed to fetch`, the gallery's patch); the Rust route answers `check/open` with an error the server does give, a bug's report, which the screen prints as the rebuild's error text (`internal error`). check-rail-empty.why: Against tC4 rc.2 (d25b7871) the rail is tC4's, its groups that fold with their counts and Fold all included (#769, REF1c), and so are the compare card (#762), the note box and the Notes titles (#773). The pixels differ where the original-language pane lights the check's words (OLH-1, built ahead of tC4 by the owner's ruling Q39, tC4 #840) and as the sentences below say. The item detail beside the rail is B5b's (captured again with its session screens): its compare card is tC4's (#762), and the sample's Learn more link reads "Translation Academy" in both. The rail is tC4's line for line but for one count: the sample's decision gr8c (Titus 1:4) is stored invalidated with no status, which tC4 shows red but leaves out of Invalid (`status === 'invalid'`), and the journal's rule (STORAGE §7.7, tc_journal::decision::assess) shows as Invalid, as tC4 shows every decision it invalidates itself. So Invalid reads 1 where tC4 reads 0, and the filter that matches nothing, which the case presses, is Bookmarked rather than Invalid. The rail header's bar carries tC4 #764's declared difference (see check-picker).

The Rust app reads the same pack list tC4 does (`pack_sentence`, the three clauses of tC4's `describePack`), so installing the pack in the scenario gives tC4's line.

gateway-change-error.why: tC4's case draws the error of a confirm made while another project is open (`gateway.otherProject`: "Another project is open now. Open this project and choose the language again."), which a Rust confirmation cannot meet: a plan belongs to the open it was made for and a confirm for another open is refused as stale before anything is written (APP-DESIGN 4.8). The reachable failure is a save the disk refuses, and the dialog states its reason in the same callout after "The change was not applied.": the capture answers the confirm with a disk with no room, "There is no room left on the disk.", so the one text line differs and every other line, style and pixel outside that line is tC4's.

section-empty-confirm.why: The save indicator reads “Unsaved changes” (`data-state="dirty"`, tone `warn`) where tC4 reads “Saved”: tC4's indicator mirrors only its verse scheduler, and a section card's text is not in it until Save, so tC4 says “Saved” while every word of the section has just been deleted and nothing is stored. The rebuild's section card is a field of the save machine (APP-DESIGN §6.5, `SaveRule::OnSaveOnly`), so the indicator says what is true: there are unsaved changes (a declared difference, docs/PLAN.md, unit B4b). Those are the only pixels that differ. In the DOM, besides the indicator's three lines, the textarea keeps the text it opened with as its child text node, where React writes each new value there too (`defaultValue`); the field's value, which is what the person sees and what is saved, is empty on both sides. Every other line of the DOM, every computed style included, is tC4's, and the question, its words, buttons and focus are tC4's.

conflict-review.why: The review of Titus 1:1 after two teammates changed it on Door43, no version selected. Every pixel and every line of the DOM, computed styles included, is tC4's but for two things. The dates of the versions: each date is when its version was made, so tC4's are its capture's time and the rebuild's are its own run's (the scripted teammates' versions carry the environment's fixed time, 1 October 2026), and the card's `data-ts` is tC4's §8.2 ts there and the rebuild's change id here. The History button under the versions (#78, read only until C7a's Restore): a rebuild-only control (Q-9) that lists every version of the verse with how it came to be. The sync that brings the teammates' versions is scripted (`test/script`, the environment's teammatesChangeOneVerse) until X; the teammates edit Door43's copy of the project, so a version this computer has not synced stays a version of its own.

cc-obs-wrapped.why: After the click on “Pictures wrapped”, React updates each layout chip's style in place, one changed property at a time: it sets the chip's new `border` shorthand, whose value holds a `var()`, and does not set the unchanged `borderWidth: 1` again after it, so tC4's DOM reads the four `border-*-width` longhands as pending (empty). The rebuild writes each chip's whole style again, so they read `1px`, as both DOMs do before the click (`cc-obs` is the same). `--stroke` is 1px, so every pixel is the same (0 differ). Unit B8.
